items.correctExplanation: Right — smooth equations never single out one result, yet labs always record one. The mismatch is the measurement problem.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — outcomes versus equations. Schrödinger evolution preserves all branches; experience delivers one — reconciling them is the field.
items.lessonContent:
Measurement pits smooth math against single outcomes.
Every interpretation answers this mismatch differently.
No experiment yet crowns a winner.
Share this: ask what 'collapse' could physically mean.
items.question: What is the quantum measurement problem?
items.title: The Vanishing Alternative

items.correctExplanation: Correct — Copenhagen assigns no path between preparations and clicks. Questions about 'which way' are ruled meaningless, not hard.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, trajectories go unmentioned. Bohr's doctrine declines to narrate unmeasured journeys.
items.lessonContent:
Copenhagen declines to narrate unmeasured paths.
Complementarity trades trajectories for predictions.
'Which way' counts as a bad question.
Share this: decline one unanswerable 'which way'.
items.question: What does the Copenhagen interpretation say about a particle's path between measurements?
items.title: The Unwritten Path

items.correctExplanation: Yes — every outcome occurs on some branch; observers split with results. Collapse is replaced by proliferation.
items.incorrectExplanation: Close! Branches, no collapse. Everett keeps one equation and pays with myriad worlds.
items.lessonContent:
Many-Worlds trades collapse for multiplicity.
Branching replaces mysterious selection.
Parsimony of equations costs worlds.
Share this: count worlds in one coin toss.
items.question: How does Many-Worlds handle measurement outcomes?
items.title: The Splitting Worlds

items.correctExplanation: Right — if everything happens, grounding 50/50 versus 99/1 needs extra machinery. Probabilities are Many-Worlds' open wound.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — why odds at all. Decision-theoretic and counting derivations all strain to recover Born weights.
items.lessonContent:
Born probabilities trouble branch-counting deeply.
Decision theory attempts rescues ambitiously.
The wound stays open after decades.
Share this: ask what odds mean if all happens.
items.question: What is the probability problem for Many-Worlds?
items.title: The Ungrounded Odds

items.correctExplanation: Correct — QBism reads quantum states as personal betting guides. Physics advises agents; reality stays unspeakable.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, beliefs, not furniture. Wavefunctions encode better wagers, not world-stuff.
items.lessonContent:
QBism personalizes quantum probabilities radically.
Agents bet; equations advise the betting.
Objectivity retreats to betting coherence.
Share this: bet explicitly on one lab outcome.
items.question: What does QBism say wavefunctions represent?
items.title: The Personal Wave

items.correctExplanation: Yes — Bohmian particles ride real waves deterministically, at the price of instant nonlocal coordination. Hidden variables survive non-locally.
items.incorrectExplanation: Close! Particles plus guiding waves. Determinate positions return; locality pays the fare.
items.lessonContent:
Pilot waves restore particles at locality's expense.
Nonlocality becomes explicit choreography.
Bell's verdict permits exactly this trade.
Share this: picture surfers on invisible swells.
items.question: How does de Broglie-Bohm theory restore determinism?
items.title: The Guided Particle

items.correctExplanation: Right — GRW adds rare random collapses, amplified for big objects. Testable deviations from textbook quantum mark it.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — spontaneous localization hits. Microscopic rarity plus macroscopic frequency solves the macro riddle.
items.lessonContent:
GRW collapses wavefunctions spontaneously and rarely.
Amplification rescues macroscopic definiteness.
Experiments can actually falsify it.
Share this: praise one testable interpretation.
items.question: What mechanism do GRW objective-collapse theories propose?
items.title: The Random Snap

items.correctExplanation: Correct — surroundings entangle with quantum phases, leaking interference away. Decoherence explains missing fringes, not chosen outcomes.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, environment steals coherence. Air and photons eavesdrop phases into unrecoverable spread.
items.lessonContent:
Decoherence leaks phases into environments.
Interference dies by eavesdropping, not minds.
Outcomes still need separate explaining.
Share this: blame air for one lost fringe.
items.question: What does decoherence explain — and what does it leave open?
items.title: The Leaking Phase

items.correctExplanation: Yes — states that survive environmental eavesdropping become classical pointer readings. Einselection elects the robust.
items.incorrectExplanation: Close! Survivors of monitoring. Position-like states endure; their superpositions dissolve.
items.lessonContent:
Einselection elects environment-proof states.
Robustness, not privilege, crowns pointers.
Classicality emerges from survivorship.
Share this: elect one survivor in daily noise.
items.question: What are pointer states in decoherence theory?
items.title: The Elected Classical

items.correctExplanation: Right — marking paths kills fringes; erasing the marks revives them. Information, not disturbance, governs interference.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — which-path knowledge toggles. Availability of path records, read or not, decides the pattern.
items.lessonContent:
Erasers restore fringes by destroying records.
Knowledge availability toggles wave behavior.
No backward causation is required.
Share this: toggle one fringe with information.
items.question: What does the quantum eraser experiment prove?
items.title: The Forgiving Eraser

items.correctExplanation: Correct — delayed choice selects which phenomenon manifests; nothing rewrites the photon's past. Context chooses the story.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, complementarity, not retrocausation. Late apparatus settings select wave or particle readings legitimately.
items.lessonContent:
Delayed choice stages complementarity dramatically.
Past events gain meaning from later contexts.
Causation still flows forward only.
Share this: stage one context-dependent reading.
items.question: Does Wheeler's delayed-choice experiment change the photon's past?
items.title: The Late Decision

items.correctExplanation: Yes — Bell correlations exceed every local-hidden-variable ceiling. Nature keeps no local ledger of outcomes.
items.incorrectExplanation: Close! Local realism dies. Experiments side with entanglement against local predetermination.
items.lessonContent:
Bell tests execute local realism experimentally.
Ceilings derived, correlations exceeded.
Nonlocality or nonrealism must give.
Share this: toast Bell's inequality slayers.
items.question: What did Bell-inequality violations rule out?
items.title: The Broken Ceiling

items.correctExplanation: Right — Kochen-Specker forbids preassigned values independent of measurement context. Questions carry their apparatus along.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — context colors results. Values crystallize with contexts; none wait preformed.
items.lessonContent:
Contextuality denies context-free properties.
Measurements co-create their outcomes.
Hidden tables cannot prelist answers.
Share this: ask what 'the' value assumes.
items.question: What does the Kochen-Specker theorem forbid?
items.title: The Contextual Verdict

items.correctExplanation: Correct — friend records a fact while Wigner describes coherent superposition. Quantum facts attach to observers.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, facts go relative. Sealed observers and super-observers tell incompatible true stories.
items.lessonContent:
Wigner's friend relativizes recorded facts.
Observers nest inside others' superpositions.
'What happened' needs a 'for whom'.
Share this: nest one observer inside another.
items.question: What paradox does Wigner's friend pose?
items.title: The Nested Observer

items.correctExplanation: Yes — extended friends force contradictions among individually reasonable assumptions. No-go theorems corner objective facts.
items.incorrectExplanation: Close! Single reality fails. Frauchiger-Renner shows consistent single-world stories breaking down.
items.lessonContent:
Extended friends corner single realities.
Reasonable assumptions collide mutually.
Something familiar must surrender.
Share this: list which assumption you'd drop.
items.question: What does the Frauchiger-Renner argument show?
items.title: The Cornered Reality

items.correctExplanation: Right — PBR proves distinct quantum states can't share underlying reality, given preparation independence. Waves are real or conspiracies reign.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — wavefunctions go ontic. Overlapping realities for distinct states collapse under the theorem.
items.lessonContent:
PBR argues wavefunctions represent reality.
Distinct states demand distinct substrates.
Epistemic readings pay conspiracy prices.
Share this: defend one wavefunction's reality.
items.question: What does the PBR theorem imply about wavefunctions?
items.title: The Real Wave

items.correctExplanation: Correct — interference verifies live bombs without detonating most. Possibilities interact where actualities don't.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, detection without touch. Counterfactual paths probe bombs that never explode.
items.lessonContent:
Bomb testers measure without interacting.
Possibility structures guide real outcomes.
Counterfactuals carry physical weight.
Share this: detect one thing without touching.
items.question: How does the Elitzur-Vaidman bomb tester work?
items.title: The Untouched Bomb

items.correctExplanation: Yes — rapid repeated measurement pins evolution. Watched quantum pots never boil.
items.incorrectExplanation: Close! Watching freezes decay. Frequent projections restart the decay clock continually.
items.lessonContent:
Zeno pins systems by frequent checking.
Projections restart evolution clocks.
Observation throttles change itself.
Share this: freeze one decay by watching.
items.question: What is the quantum Zeno effect?
items.title: The Frozen Decay

items.correctExplanation: Right — recorded which-path information destroys interference even unread. Erasure, not ignorance, restores waves.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — records kill fringes. Existing path records collapse patterns; destroyed ones revive them.
items.lessonContent:
Records, read or not, kill interference.
Existence of information decides patterns.
Ignorance alone restores nothing.
Share this: guard one secret path-mark.
items.question: Do unread which-path detectors still destroy interference?
items.title: The Unread Record

items.correctExplanation: Correct — Schrödinger mocked applying quantum rules to cats. Absurdity indicts uncritical scaling, not felines.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, reductio of macro-superposition. The cat dramatizes measurement's unfinished business.
items.lessonContent:
Schrödinger's cat mocks naive scaling.
Thought experiments indict missing theories.
Absurdity signals explanatory gaps.
Share this: free one cat with decoherence.
items.question: What was Schrödinger's cat intended to show?
items.title: The Mocked Feline

items.correctExplanation: Yes — von Neumann showed the collapse cut slides along the measurement chain arbitrarily. Placements are conventional, never forced.
items.incorrectExplanation: Close! Cut floats anywhere. Eye, retina, or apparatus — mathematics works at every station.
items.lessonContent:
Von Neumann chains slide cuts freely.
No station hosts collapse necessarily.
Conventions choose; physics stays silent.
Share this: slide one cut along a chain.
items.question: Where must the Heisenberg cut be placed?
items.title: The Sliding Cut

items.correctExplanation: Right — environments broadcast many copies of pointer states; consensus builds objectivity. Redundancy manufactures classical agreement.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — redundant environmental copies. Photons scatter identical records widely; observers sample the consensus.
items.lessonContent:
Quantum Darwinism objectifies via redundancy.
Many copies let many observers agree.
Fittest states replicate environmentally.
Share this: sample one consensus reality.
items.question: How does quantum Darwinism explain objective reality?
items.title: The Broadcast Reality

items.correctExplanation: Correct — C60 buckyballs show double-slit fringes. Quantum waves scale far past atoms.
items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, molecules interfere too. Sixty-atom carbon cages diffract like electrons.
items.lessonContent:
Buckyballs diffract like electrons do.
Macroscopic quantumness is laboratory routine.
Size limits keep retreating upward.
Share this: picture soccer-ball interference.
items.question: What did C60 buckyball interference prove?
items.title: The Giant Fringe

items.correctExplanation: Yes — environmental monitoring explains missing macro-superpositions without minds. Consciousness retired from physics duty.
items.incorrectExplanation: Close! Decoherence suffices instead. Eavesdropping air collapses appearances mindlessly.
items.lessonContent:
Consciousness-collapse theories largely retired.
Environments monitor ceaselessly instead.
Minds observe outcomes; they don't author them.
Share this: retire one mystical collapse tale.
items.question: Why did consciousness-causes-collapse fall from favor?
items.title: The Retired Mind

items.correctExplanation: Right — superdeterminism saves locality by denying measurement independence. Cosmic conspiracy scripts settings and outcomes jointly.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — freedom-of-choice loophole. Correlated settings and hidden variables conspire from the Big Bang.
items.lessonContent:
Superdeterminism sacrifices experimenter freedom.
Cosmic scripts correlate settings with states.
Freedom costs locality's last hope.
Share this: price one conspiracy theory fairly.

items.title: The Cosmic Script
